title: Weigh each portable football goal down on its rear ground bar, behind the line it would tip over
instruction: Weigh the two goals down with the sandbags.
context: A portable football goal tips forward onto anyone who hangs from its crossbar unless its back is held down: tip-overs have killed more than 30 people in the US since 1979, mostly children, and the US Consumer Product Safety Commission tells schools and clubs to anchor or counterweight every movable goal at all times. A bag on the grass does nothing, and a bag at the front posts sits on the line the goal tips over, so it barely resists; the weight has to lie on the rear ground bar, behind that line. The two goals here face opposite ways, so the rear bar is the far bar of one and the near bar of the other. The robot has to work out from the camera which way each goal faces, carry a bag past the frame and rest it on a 3 cm bar. The instruction does not say where the bags go. Done by: PE teachers, groundskeepers and coaches.
setup: A green pitch (46 x 84 cm) on the table has two model goals (16 cm wide, 7.5 cm tall posts, white), each with a ground frame 9 cm deep and a 3 cm rear ground bar. The left goal, 17 cm left of centre, has its mouth toward the arms at 27 cm out and its rear bar at 36 cm out; the right goal, 17 cm right, faces away, with its mouth at 36 cm out and its rear bar at 27 cm. White penalty box lines and a spot on the grass show which way each goal faces. Two sandbags (4 x 9 x 2 cm, 150 g, tan with a dark 1.8 x 1.8 x 3 cm strap loop) lie 36 cm left and 36 cm right of centre, 18 cm out. Also: a football, three cones and a water crate beyond the goals.
scoring: A goal counts as anchored when a sandbag lies at rest on its rear ground bar: its centre over the bar (within 1.5 cm front to back and inside the goal's 16 cm width), resting flat on it (tilted less than 10 degrees, within 5 mm of the bar's top height). 0.5 for each anchored goal; either bag may go on either goal. Scored at the end.
reset_notes: Lift the sandbags off the goals and set them back on their marks 36 cm to each side; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Scale models: the goals are rigid and fixed to the table, so a goal with no weight on it never actually tips in the simulation. The scorer checks what a groundskeeper checks: ballast resting on the rear ground bar of each goal.
